rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results (Figs 1-9) - the authors report their own laboratory incubations of two agricultural soils (loamy silt T1, sandy silt V1) measuring NO and N2O release by nitrification and denitrification under varying O2 partial pressure and soil moisture content.
rows.notes: The study contains no irrigation treatment and no crop yield or crop production data. It is a laboratory incubation (5-10 g soil in serum bottles) measuring trace gas release. The only result bearing on the claim is a precondition: the fine-textured loamy silt showed N2O release by denitrification starting at a lower soil moisture content than the coarse-textured sandy silt, which the authors interpret as the fine soil becoming anoxic at lower moisture (Discussion, Fig. 6). This supports the 'poor aeration in fine-textured soils' premise but says nothing about drip versus subsurface drip irrigation or yield gaps. Hence Q2 is no; upstream and technology mismatch flagged. Note the review cites it as 2004 but the paper is Global Change Biology 1998.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a two-soil laboratory incubation on NO/N2O release; no irrigation technology or crop production is studied.
